mainTopic: How עירוב חצירות and שיתוף מבואות work together according to רבי מאיר, and why רב left 'opening into one another' out of the משנה.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about carrying in courtyards and an alleyway (מבוי). An עירוב חצירות joins the houses of one courtyard, and a שיתוף מבואות joins the courtyards that open into one alleyway. If both are made, carrying is allowed everywhere. If one courtyard resident forgot the עירוב but joined the שיתוף, carrying is still allowed everywhere. If one alleyway resident skipped the שיתוף, only the alleyway is forbidden. The גמרא says the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף. After challenges that the משנה seems to switch to רבנן, it explains that רבי מאיר requires an עירוב only so children do not forget it. When most residents made one, that concern does not apply. The גמרא then reports that רב's version of the משנה left out 'courtyards opening into one another.' רב יוסף explains that a שיתוף's food must pass through the alleyway. That explanation is defended against two משניות but refuted by רבה בר חנן. The גמרא then gives a new reason: an alleyway needs houses and courtyards opening into it. It begins examining that rule of רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the alleyway is joined, carrying is allowed everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the courtyards also made a שיתוף in the מבוי, people may carry both in the courtyards and in the alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they joined together in the alleyway, they are allowed to carry here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. It has just said that an עירוב in the courtyards alone is not enough for the alleyway. Now it adds that if they also made a שיתוף in the מבוי, carrying is allowed in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyards were already permitted because each one made its own עירוב חצירות. The new piece is the שיתוף מבואות, which joins all the courtyards into one unit along the alleyway. That unlocks the alleyway too. So 'here and there' means the courtyards and the alleyway.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that several courtyards open into
They joined together, meaning they made a שיתוף
Joining all the courtyards of an alleyway so that people may carry in the alleyway
Here and there, meaning both the courtyards and the alleyway

phrases.english: And if they joined together in the alleyway
phrases.notes: This refers to a שיתוף made in addition to the courtyard עירובין.

phrases.english: they are permitted here and there.
phrases.notes: Carrying is allowed in both the courtyards and the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf, which said that an עירוב in the courtyards alone permits only the courtyards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both עירוב חצירות and שיתוף מבואות are made, carrying is permitted in the courtyards and in the alleyway.

steps.title: A courtyard resident forgot the courtyard עירוב
steps.stepSummary: Both an עירוב and a שיתוף were made, but one courtyard resident forgot to join the עירוב. Carrying is still permitted everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they made an עירוב in the courtyards and joined together in the alleyway, and one of the courtyard residents forgot and did not join the עירוב, they are permitted here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where one person missed the courtyard עירוב but did join the alleyway שיתוף. It rules that everyone may still carry in the courtyards and in the alleyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, one courtyard resident who is left out of the עירוב forbids carrying in that courtyard. Here he did join the bigger alleyway שיתוף. That larger joining covers him, so it works in place of the courtyard עירוב he missed.

keyTerms.meaning: Joining the houses of one courtyard so that people may carry in the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two tools. The עירוב is for the courtyard and the שיתוף is for the alleyway. In this case the person missed the smaller one (the עירוב), and the bigger one (the שיתוף) saves the day.

phrases.english: If they made an עירוב in the courtyards
phrases.notes: Each courtyard made its own עירוב.

phrases.english: and they joined together in the alleyway,
phrases.notes: A שיתוף was also made for the alleyway.

phrases.english: and one of the residents of a courtyard forgot
and did not join the עירוב
phrases.notes: He did join the שיתוף.

phrases.english: they are permitted here and there.
phrases.notes: The שיתוף covers his missing עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵירְבוּ בַּחֲצֵירוֹת וְנִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בַּמָּבוֹי, וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where one person is missing from the courtyard עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שיתוף מבואות that includes a resident can work in place of the courtyard עירוב that he forgot to join.

steps.title: An alleyway resident did not join the שיתוף
steps.stepSummary: If one alleyway resident did not join the שיתוף, carrying is allowed in the courtyards but forbidden in the alleyway. The reason is that an alleyway relates to its courtyards the way a courtyard relates to its houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the alleyway residents did not join the שיתוף, they are permitted in the courtyards and forbidden in the alleyway, because the alleyway is to the courtyards like the courtyard is to the houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case, where someone missed the alleyway שיתוף. The alleyway becomes forbidden, but the courtyards stay permitted, and the משנה states the principle behind this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyards still have their own עירובין, so carrying in them is fine. The alleyway, though, works like a big courtyard shared by all the courtyards. Just as one house left out of the עירוב forbids a courtyard, one resident left out of the שיתוף forbids the alleyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The alleyway is to the courtyards like the courtyard is to the houses

steps.whatToRemember: Two levels, one model: houses join into a courtyard through an עירוב, and courtyards join into an alleyway through a שיתוף. Missing the upper level forbids only the upper area.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle that an alleyway is like a courtyard for its courtyards lets us apply all the courtyard rules to the alleyway, one level up.

phrases.english: [If one] of the residents of the alleyway [forgot] and did not join the שיתוף
phrases.notes: The words 'forgot one' carry over from the previous case.

phrases.english: they are permitted in the courtyards
phrases.notes: The courtyards still have their own עירובין.

phrases.english: and forbidden in the alleyway,
because the alleyway is to the courtyards
like the courtyard is to the houses.
phrases.notes: The guiding principle of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 2: the שיתוף is missing instead of the עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missing שיתוף forbids carrying in the alleyway only. The courtyards stay permitted because they work like houses opening into a shared courtyard.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא this משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking who the author of this משנה is. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף. That is a position not everyone holds, so the גמרא wants to name the authority behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Who is it, meaning whose opinion is this

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Whose [view] is it?
phrases.notes: A standard question asking who wrote the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא's analysis of it.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר, who requires both
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that both an עירוב and a שיתוף are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, who said: we need an עירוב and we need a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה builds its cases on both an עירוב in the courtyards and a שיתוף in the alleyway (עירבו בחצירות ונשתתפו במבוי), which implies that both are needed. That fits רבי מאיר, who requires both tools. רבנן hold that one is enough, so at first glance the משנה cannot follow them.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי מאיר: both an עירוב and a שיתוף are needed.

phrases.english: It is רבי מאיר,
who said:
We require an עירוב
phrases.notes: This is for the courtyards.

phrases.english: and we require a שיתוף.
phrases.notes: This is for the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: בָּעִינַן עֵירוּב וּבָעִינַן שִׁיתּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף.

steps.title: The middle clause seems to follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The middle clause of the משנה permits carrying once a שיתוף was made. That sounds like the רבנן, who say one is enough, and not like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the middle clause: 'If they made a שיתוף in the alleyway, carrying is permitted here and there.' Now we are holding like the רבנן, who say one (a שיתוף alone) is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. It points to a clause that seems to need only a שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires both an עירוב in each courtyard and a שיתוף in the alleyway. The middle clause mentions only the שיתוף and already allows carrying everywhere. That fits the רבנן, who hold that one of the two is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We have arrived at (the opinion of)...

phrases.english: Say the middle clause:
"And if they merged in the alleyway,
they are permitted here and there"
we have arrived at the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The clause now seems to follow the רבנן.

phrases.english: who say one is enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 5 that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle clause allows carrying with a שיתוף alone, which matches the רבנן and not רבי מאיר

steps.title: Read the middle clause as 'also merged'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that they also made a שיתוף, in addition to the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. The משנה means: 'And if they ALSO made a שיתוף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the middle clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clause is not saying a שיתוף alone works. It is adding the שיתוף on top of the courtyard עירובין already mentioned. So both were made, which fits רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: That is not difficult:
it is saying 'and if they also merged.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle clause permits carrying with a שיתוף alone
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause means a שיתוף in addition to the עירוב, so it fits רבי מאיר

steps.title: In the next clause, the forgetful courtyard resident must have renounced his rights
steps.stepSummary: Carrying is permitted even though one courtyard resident did not join the עירוב. The only way this works is if he gave up his rights (ביטול רשות).
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the next clause: 'They made עירובין in the courtyards and a שיתוף in the alleyway, and one courtyard resident forgot and did not join the עירוב. Carrying is permitted here and there.' What is the case? If he did not give up his rights, why is carrying permitted? It must be obvious that he did give them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down what case the next clause is talking about. It is setting up a problem for the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One person who is not part of the עירוב normally forbids carrying for everyone in the courtyard. Since the משנה permits carrying, he must have done ביטול רשות, giving up his rights to the others. This conclusion is the premise for the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a final ruling. The גמרא is only proving that the person renounced his rights so that it can ask a question on the last clause in the next step.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
They made an eiruv in the courtyards and merged in the alleyway,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר וְלֹא עֵירַב —
phrases.english: and one of the courtyard residents forgot and did not join the eiruv
they are permitted here and there.
What are the circumstances?
If he did not renounce his rights,
why are they permitted?
Rather, it is obvious that he renounced.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (first half of a two-part challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: עֵירְבוּ בַּחֲצֵירוֹת וְנִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בַּמָּבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues checking the משנה clause by clause and sets up the next challenge
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the case in which carrying is permitted despite the forgetful resident?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He must have renounced his rights (ביטול רשות)

steps.title: If renunciation works, why is the alleyway forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: In the last clause, one alleyway resident forgot the שיתוף and carrying in the alleyway is forbidden. If he renounced his rights, why is it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last clause: 'One alleyway resident forgot and did not join the שיתוף. Carrying is permitted in the courtyards and forbidden in the alleyway.' But if he renounced his rights, why is carrying forbidden in the alleyway?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the conclusion of Step 8 to challenge the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the forgetful courtyard resident is assumed to have renounced, the forgetful alleyway resident should be treated the same way. Renunciation should then permit the alleyway too. Yet the משנה forbids it, so the clauses seem inconsistent.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי מָבוֹי וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ —
phrases.english: one of the alleyway residents forgot and they did not merge
they are permitted in the courtyards
and forbidden in the alleyway.
But if he renounced
why are they forbidden in the alleyway?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the premise from Step 8 to attack the last clause
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the last clause that carrying in the alleyway is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ביטול רשות is assumed in the courtyard case, it should also apply in the alleyway case and permit carrying

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי מאיר holds renunciation does not work in an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: A possible answer is offered: רבי מאיר holds that ביטול רשות is not effective in a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי מאיר holds there is no renunciation of rights in an alleyway...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer, but only in order to reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would explain the difference: ביטול works in a courtyard but not in an alleyway. Then the forgetful alleyway resident still forbids carrying. The phrase וכי תימא signals that this answer is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggested answer that will be rejected)
Renouncing one's rights to a shared area

steps.confusionAlert: וכי תימא is not the גמרא's final answer. It introduces an answer that the גמרא will immediately disprove.

phrases.english: And if you say
Rabbi Meir holds
there is no renunciation of rights in an alleyway.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Part of the following דחיה (a proposed answer set up for rejection)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between courtyard and alleyway regarding ביטול רשות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Renunciation should permit carrying in the alleyway
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, renunciation does not work in a מבוי (a suggestion that will be rejected)

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר accepts renunciation in an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying 'he renounced his rights in your favor' about an alleyway, so the suggested answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'For he renounced his rights to you.' These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of Step 10 by quoting a ברייתא. The question from Step 9 comes back, and the next step responds to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר does accept ביטול רשות in a מבוי. So the suggested answer cannot explain why the alleyway is forbidden. The next step takes a different approach.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (in a ברייתא)?
For he has renounced his rights to you

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא proved that the forgetful courtyard resident renounced his rights. It then asked why renunciation does not also permit the alleyway. The answer 'no ביטול in a מבוי according to רבי מאיר' was rejected by a ברייתא. The next step responds by dropping the assumption of ביטול רשות altogether.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
"For he renounced his rights in your favor,"
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי מאיר holds there is no ביטול רשות in a מבוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר accepting ביטול רשות in an alleyway

steps.title: The alleyway resident did not renounce, so the courtyard resident did not renounce either
steps.stepSummary: After the rejected answer, the גמרא concludes that in the last clause the man simply did not renounce his rights. It infers that the clause about the courtyard resident who forgot the עירוב also involves no ביטול רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he did not renounce his rights. And since the last clause is a case where he did not renounce, the earlier clause is also a case where he did not renounce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea of ביטול רשות entirely. It reads both clauses as cases where nobody renounced anything, and this sets up a new difficulty in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the alleyway case was forbidden, which shows that resident did not renounce. Clauses that sit side by side should be read the same way. So when the courtyard resident forgot the עירוב, carrying was permitted with no ביטול רשות at all. That can only work if the alleyway's שיתוף also counts as the courtyard's עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רישא' means the clause just before the סיפא: the courtyard resident who forgot the עירוב. In the next step, 'רישא, מציעתא, סיפא' divide the whole משנה into three parts, so the same word points to a different clause.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that he did not renounce.
And since the last clause is where he did not renounce,
the earlier clause is also where he did not renounce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the answer in step 10 was rejected in step 11, the גמרא now accepts that no ביטול רשות happened.
steps.raayaObject: That the clause where a courtyard resident forgot the עירוב involves no ביטול רשות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel structure with the סיפא, where carrying is forbidden and so clearly no ביטול רשות took place

steps.title: The משנה seems split between two opinions
steps.stepSummary: If the שיתוף alone permits the courtyards, that is the view of רבנן. But the other clauses follow רבי מאיר, so the משנה would switch authors in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause and the last clause follow רבי מאיר, and the middle clause follows רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an awkward result: one משנה would follow two different authors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires both an עירוב and a שיתוף. רבנן hold that a שיתוף can also serve as the courtyard's עירוב. The middle clause permits the courtyards without an עירוב from everyone and without ביטול רשות, which fits רבנן. The surrounding clauses fit רבי מאיר, and a משנה is not normally split this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view against רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: The first and last clauses are Rabbi Meir,
and the middle clause is the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, מְצִיעֲתָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inference of step 12 to show that the משנה would have two different authors.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה's authorship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permitting the courtyards through the שיתוף alone is the view of רבנן, while the other clauses require both, like רבי מאיר. A single משנה should not jump between authors.

steps.title: The whole משנה follows רבי מאיר because his reason does not apply here
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר requires an עירוב in addition to the שיתוף only so that children will not forget the laws of עירוב. When most residents made an עירוב, there is no such risk, so even רבי מאיר permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר. What is רבי מאיר's reason for requiring both an עירוב and a שיתוף? So that the law of עירוב will not be forgotten by the children. Here, since most of them made an עירוב, it will not be forgotten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the middle clause also fits רבי מאיר. It does this by explaining the reason behind his requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees that a שיתוף could legally cover the courtyards. He demands a separate עירוב only as a safeguard for education. Once most residents made an עירוב, the children still see it being done, so the safeguard is not needed. That is why carrying is permitted even though one person forgot.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's double requirement (עירוב plus שיתוף) is an educational safeguard so children don't forget עירוב. Where most residents made an עירוב, the safeguard is not needed and he permits.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic requirement can have limits built into its purpose. When the reason behind it is absent, a lenient outcome follows even for the stricter view.

phrases.english: It is all Rabbi Meir,
and what is the reason Rabbi Meir said
we require an eiruv and we require a merging of alleyways?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁכֵּחַ תּוֹרַת עֵירוּב מִן הַתִּינוֹקוֹת,
phrases.english: So as not to cause the law of eiruv to be forgotten by the children,
and here, since most of them made an eiruv,
it will not be forgotten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by reading the middle clause according to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind a view to limit how far it applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed that רבי מאיר always requires an actual עירוב from everyone, so the middle clause must follow רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's requirement is only a safeguard against forgetting. When most residents made an עירוב, he agrees the courtyards are permitted, so the whole משנה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב's version of the משנה leaves out 'opening into one another'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that רב did not include the words 'opening into one another' in the משנה. רב כהנא reports the same. Another version says רב כהנא himself did not include these words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: רב did not teach 'opening into one another.' And so too רב כהנא said: רב did not teach 'opening into one another.' Some say: רב כהנא himself did not teach 'opening into one another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the exact wording of the משנה. It reports that רב's version said the courtyards open only into the alleyway, not into each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in our text describes five courtyards that open into one another and also into the alleyway. רב left out the first part, so in his version each courtyard opens only into the alleyway. The 'איכא דאמרי' gives a second version: this text came from רב כהנא himself rather than being reported in רב's name.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not teach / did not include in his version of the text
Opening into one another (courtyards connected directly)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Rav did not teach 'open into one another.'
And so too Rav Kahana said:
Rav did not teach 'open into one another.'
Some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא גּוּפֵיהּ לָא תָּנֵי ״פְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ״.
phrases.english: Rav Kahana himself did not teach 'open into one another.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: רַב לָא תָּנֵי פְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the authorship question, the גמרא turns to a textual variant in the משנה's opening case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב's version, the courtyards in the משנה do not open into one another. They open only into the alleyway.

steps.title: אביי asks why רב left out those words
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what reason רב had for not including 'opening into one another.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is the reason he did not teach 'opening into one another'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks for the reasoning behind רב's version of the text. This sets up רב יוסף's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Courtyards that open into each other do not seem to change the laws of עירוב and שיתוף in any obvious way. So אביי wants to know what problem those words would create.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, the student questioning רב יוסף

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is the reason he did not teach
'open into one another'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the textual report of step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב's version of the משנה leaves out the courtyards opening into one another

steps.title: A שיתוף must pass through the alleyway's entrances
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רב holds a שיתוף is valid only if its food is brought in and out through the entrances to the alleyway. If the courtyards open into each other, the food might be passed directly between them, and the שיתוף would be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that any שיתוף that is not brought in and taken out through the entrances to the alleyway is not considered a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by giving the rule behind רב's version of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיתוף joins the alleyway, so its food has to travel by way of the alleyway. If the food goes straight from one courtyard to another, it looks like a courtyard עירוב instead of an alleyway שיתוף, and it does not work as a שיתוף. Courtyards that open into each other invite that direct transfer, so רב taught the משנה without that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings it in and takes it out
Is not called / is not considered

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a שיתוף is only valid if its food passes through the alleyway's entrances. Food passed directly from courtyard to courtyard does not count as a שיתוף.

phrases.english: He holds that any merging of alleyways
that one does not bring in and take out
by way of the entrances into the alleyway
is not considered a merging of alleyways.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר כׇּל שִׁיתּוּף שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסוֹ וּמוֹצִיאוֹ דֶּרֶךְ פְּתָחִים בַּמָּבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שיתוף must be carried in and out through the alleyway's entrances. Courtyards that open into each other risk a direct transfer, which would make the שיתוף invalid, so רב left out 'opening into one another.'

steps.title: Challenge from the homeowner partnered with his neighbors in wine
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that a homeowner who shares wine with his neighbors does not need an עירוב. It says nothing about the wine being carried through the מבוי, which seems to contradict רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors, with this one in wine and with that one in wine, they do not need to make an עירוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner (apparently אביי) quotes a משנה to challenge רב יוסף's explanation of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, jointly owned wine works as a שיתוף, and no one mentions carrying it out into the alleyway and back. That suggests the food does not need to travel through the מבוי entrances, which goes against the rule given in Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Partner, a co-owner of the food

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: He's challenging him with a teaching from the תנאים.

phrases.english: A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors,
with this one in wine and with that one in wine,
they do not need to make an eiruv.
phrases.notes: Nothing here mentions taking the wine out to the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason רב יוסף gave for רב in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that the food of a שיתוף must be taken out to the מבוי and brought back in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes shared wine valid without mentioning that it went through the alleyway, so that seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The wine there was taken out and brought back in
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking about a case where the wine was in fact carried out to the alleyway and then brought back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where they took it out and brought it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply did not mention the detail. It is assumed that the wine did pass through the alleyway, so רב's requirement was met.

keyTerms.meaning: They took it out (to the מבוי) and brought it in

phrases.english: There, it is where they took it out and brought it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows the wine works without going through the alleyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to wine that was taken out and brought back in, so it fits רב.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה of how to make a שיתוף in an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה describes how to make a שיתוף in a מבוי. One person acquires the food for everyone, and nothing is said about the food passing through each courtyard and the alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'How does one make a שיתוף in an alleyway?' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge is brought from the משנה that describes the procedure for a שיתוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה lets one person set down the food and acquire it on behalf of all the residents of the alleyway. It mentions no requirement to carry the food out to the מבוי and back in.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
How does one merge in an alleyway? etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of that משנה describes one person acquiring the food for all the residents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second challenge against רב's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement that the food go out to the alleyway and come back in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The standard procedure for a שיתוף does not include passing the food through the alleyway.

steps.title: There too, the food was taken out and brought back in
steps.stepSummary: The same answer is given: the משנה refers to food that was taken out of the courtyards into the alleyway and then brought in.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is where they took it out and brought it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge with the same narrowing of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the detail of passing through the alleyway is assumed even though the משנה does not mention it. So both משניות can fit רב's view.

phrases.english: There too: it is where they took it out and brought it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 the same way Step 19 answered Step 18.
steps.terutzMaskana: The procedure in that משנה assumes the food was taken out to the alleyway and brought back in.

steps.title: Would bread given over in one's basket not count as a שיתוף?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנן objects. If the food must go out to the alleyway, then a person who transfers ownership of bread sitting in his basket would not have made a valid שיתוף. That sounds unreasonable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנן objected: 'But according to this, if he transferred ownership of bread in his basket to him, would it also not be a שיתוף?!'
steps.whatsHappening: A new and sharper challenge begins. It argues that רב's rule leads to an unlikely result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread in someone's basket never travels through the alleyway. If רב's rule is correct, giving the residents a share in it would not work as a שיתוף, and רבה בר חנן finds that hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it (an Amora's challenge from logic)
But according to this... (pushing an idea to its result)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ḥanan strongly objected to it:
But if that is so,
if he transferred ownership of bread in his basket to him,
would it also not be a merging?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; of course it should count.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two challenges from משניות were answered, a new challenge from logic is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule as explained by רב יוסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule would make even bread handed over in a basket fail as a שיתוף, which seems wrong.

steps.title: רב himself lets the bread on the table count
steps.stepSummary: Someone might simply accept the result. To block that, רבה בר חנן quotes רב: when שבת begins while a group is eating, they may rely on the bread on the table as an עירוב, and some say as a שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, but didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: 'A group that was eating together when the day became holy for them may rely on the bread on the table as an עירוב.' And some say: as a שיתוף.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר חנן blocks the reply 'yes, it really would not count' by bringing a ruling from רב himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread on the table never went out to the alleyway, yet רב lets it count. This sets up a contradiction between two teachings of רב. The next step makes the contradiction sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (blocking a possible reply)
Members of a group eating together
The day became holy for them (שבת began)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse עירוב with שיתוף. An עירוב joins the houses that open into one courtyard. A שיתוף joins the courtyards that open into the same alleyway (מבוי).

phrases.english: And if you say: so it is indeed,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
members of a group who were dining together
and the day became sanctified for them —
the bread that is on the table
they may rely on it as an eiruv,
and some say it: as a merging.
phrases.notes: There are two versions of רב's teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the challenge of Step 22 with a source from רב himself.
steps.raayaObject: Food does not need to pass through the alleyway to count as a שיתוף
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling about the bread on the table, reported by רב יהודה

steps.title: רבה: eating in a house versus eating in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the two versions of רב's ruling do not argue. If the group ate in a house, the bread counts as an עירוב. If they ate in a courtyard, it counts as a שיתוף. So bread that never left the courtyard still works as a שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: 'They do not disagree. Here, when they were eating in a house. There, when they were eating in a courtyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה's explanation of רב's ruling completes רבה בר חנן's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both versions are true, there is a case where bread in a courtyard counts as a שיתוף even though it never went out to the alleyway and back. That directly contradicts the rule רב יוסף attributed to רב in Step 17, and the challenge stays open for the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: Two challenges from משניות were answered with 'it was taken out and brought in.' But רב's own teaching about bread on the table in a courtyard shows that food can count as a שיתוף without going through the alleyway. The next step answers this sharp contradiction to רב יוסף's explanation by giving a new reason for רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The house/courtyard split turns a disagreement between versions into a clear case that clashes with the requirement to take the food out and bring it in.

phrases.english: And Rabba said: they do not disagree:
here, where they were dining in a house,
phrases.notes: Food in a house serves as an עירוב for the courtyard.

phrases.english: there, where they were dining in a courtyard.
phrases.notes: Food in a courtyard serves as a שיתוף for the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof of Step 23 by showing that the שיתוף version refers to bread in a courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two versions of רב do not conflict: bread eaten in a house counts as an עירוב, and bread eaten in a courtyard counts as a שיתוף.

steps.title: A new reason for רב's reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retracts its earlier explanation. It says רב's real reason is that a מבוי cannot be permitted through a לחי or קורה unless houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רב's real reason: he holds that an alleyway cannot be made permitted through a side post and a cross beam unless there are houses and courtyards opening into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us the גמרא is dropping its earlier answer, because רבה בר חנן's objection just knocked it down. It now gives a different reason why רב did not teach the משנה as courtyards that open into one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old answer said the food had to go out into the alleyway. רבה showed that bread which never left the courtyard still works as a שיתוף, so that answer no longer stands. The new reason is about the alleyway itself: if the courtyards open into each other, they count as one big courtyard, and a מבוי needs several houses and courtyards opening into it before a לחי or קורה can permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous explanation is being dropped.
A side post placed at the entrance of an alleyway
A cross beam placed over the entrance of an alleyway

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. The earlier explanation was about whether the food reaches the alleyway. The new reason has nothing to do with the food. It is about whether the alleyway qualifies for a לחי or קורה at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the discussion away from how the שיתוף food is handled. It focuses instead on the basic requirements for an alleyway to become permitted. That sets up the גופא discussion that comes next.

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of Rav
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means we're dropping the earlier explanation, since רבה בר חנן knocked it down.

phrases.english: is that he holds:
an alleyway is not permitted through a side post and cross beam
unless there are houses and courtyards
opening into it.
phrases.notes: Courtyards that open into each other count as one courtyard, so they would not meet this requirement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that רבה בר חנן refuted in steps 22–24 with a new reason for רב's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and replacement of the earlier reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב required the food to pass through the alleyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's real concern is that an alleyway needs houses and courtyards opening into it. Courtyards that open into each other count as one, so the alleyway would not qualify.

steps.title: Looking at רב's alleyway rule on its own
steps.stepSummary: With the word גופא, the גמרא begins a separate discussion of רב's statement about which alleyways can be permitted through a לחי or קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב said: an alleyway is not permitted through a side post and cross beam...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It goes back to quote רב's rule in full so it can examine it directly, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רב's rule was used only as a tool to explain his reading of the משנה. גופא means the גמרא will now study that rule for its own sake, starting with its exact wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. It introduces a direct examination of a statement that was quoted earlier in passing.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav said:
An alleyway is not permitted through a side post and cross beam
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the rule of רב cited in step 25 and opens a new discussion of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: an alleyway cannot be permitted through a לחי or קורה unless the required conditions are met. The full wording continues on the next amud.
